([[Wilbraham, Massachusetts]]) | college = [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]] (2022–2024) | highlights = * Consensus second-team [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] ([[2024 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|2024]]) * First-team [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-ACC]] (2024) * Second-team All-ACC (2023) * [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] All-Freshman team (2023) * [[Atlantic Coast Conference Men's Basketball Rookie of the Year|ACC Rookie of the Year]] (2023) * [[ACC men's basketball tournament|ACC tournament]] MVP ([[2023 ACC men's basketball tournament|2023]]) * [[Jordan Brand Classic]] (2022) * [[Nike Hoop Summit]] (2022) }} '''Kyle Jarred "Flip" Filipowski''' (born November 7, 2003) is an American [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for the [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke Blue Devils]]. He was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2022 class. ==High school career== Filipowski first attended [[Minisink Valley High School]] in [[Slate Hill, New York]]. He transferred after his freshman year to [[Fordham Preparatory School]] in [[The Bronx]]. After his sophomore year, he transferred to [[Wilbraham & Monson Academy]] in [[Wilbraham, Massachusetts]].{{Cite web|url=https://www.masslive.com/hoophallclassic/2022/01/kyle-filipowski-shines-for-wilbraham-monson-academy-in-win-over-life-christian-academy-at-hoophall-classic.html|title = Kyle Filipowski shines for Wilbraham & Monson Academy in win over Life Christian Academy at Hoophall Classic|date = January 17, 2022}} He was the [[Gatorade Basketball Player of the Year]] for Massachusetts in 2021.{{Cite web|url=https://www.masslive.com/highschoolsports/2021/06/wilbraham-monson-academys-kyle-filipowski-named-2020-21-gatorade-massachusetts-boys-basketball-player-of-the-year.html|title=Wilbraham & Monson Academy's Kyle Filipowski named 2020-21 Gatorade Massachusetts Boys Basketball Player of the Year|date=June 8, 2021}} He was ineligible to play in the [[2022 McDonald's All-American Boys Game]] due to being a fifth-year player.{{Cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/duke/basketball/jon-scheyer-three-mcdonalds-all-americans|title=Three Jon Scheyer Recruits Named McDonald's All-Americans|date=January 26, 2022 }}{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/33145674/duke-men-basketball-prospect-dereck-lively-headlines-star-studded-roster-mcdonald-all-american-game|title = Lively headlines McDonald's All American roster|date = January 25, 2022}} ===Recruiting=== Filipowski was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and one of the top players in the 2022 class, according to major recruiting services. web|url=https://theacc.com/news/2023/12/18/dukes-filipowski-gts-ndongo-claim-acc-mens-basketball-weekly-honors.aspx|title=Duke's Filipowski, GT's Ndongo Claim ACC Men's Basketball Weekly web|url=https://goduke.com/news/2024/1/9/mens-basketball-no-11-duke-catches-fire-defeats-pitt-75-53.aspx|title=No.11 Duke Catches Fire, Defeats Pitt, 75-53|date=January 9, 2024|website=GoDuke.com|publisher=[[Duke Blue Devils]]|access-date=January 10, 2024}} On January 13, 2024, Filipowski scored a career high 30 points and 13 rebounds in a 84–79 win over [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401604121|title=Kyle Filipowski scores 30 points to help No.11 Duke top Georgia Tech 84-79|date=January 13, 2024|website=[[ESPN.com]]|publisher=[[Associated Press]]|access-date=January 25, 2024}} On February 24, 2024, Filipowski suffered an apparent knee injury in a collision with a Wake Forest fan participating in a court storming after the Demon Deacons upset the eighth-ranked Blue Devils.{{Cite web |date=February 24, 2024 |title=Duke's Filipowski injured by fan after Wake's win |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/39591762/duke-kyle-filipowski-injured-fan-wake-court-storming-win |access-date=February 25, 2024 |website=ESPN.com |language=en}} After calls to ban court storming by Duke head coach [[Jon Scheyer]], Filipowski was able to play in the next game on February 28.{{cite web|url=https://www.dukechronicle.com/article/2024/02/duke-mens-basketball-kyle-filipowski-playing-versus-louisville-wake-forest-court-storming|title=Filipowski starts for Duke men's basketball against Louisville after injury in Wake Forest court storm|last=Long|first=Andrew|date=February 28, 2024|website=[[Duke Chronicle]]|access-date=April 6, 2024}} On April 13, 2024, Filipowski declared
